captions.detailed: A set of miniature building blocks and a matching grid-patterned baseplate, similar to Ministeck toy components. The set includes a single square block with a central cylindrical peg, a double-length block with two pegs, a triple-length block with three pegs, a 2x2 square block with four pegs, and an L-shaped corner block with three pegs. The square baseplate features a hollowed-out grid underneath, consisting of square sockets designed to receive the cylindrical pegs of the blocks.
captions.instruction: Design a highly parametric toy building block set in OpenSCAD with a customizable grid baseplate. The script must allow users to adjust the size of a single block unit, the block thickness, and the peg length, while generating single, double, triple, corner, and 2x2 multi-peg blocks alongside a baseplate with matching square grid sockets.
captions.factory: The design is built around a modular `CreateSingleBlock` module, which combines a flat square `cube` of size `single_piece_size` and thickness `block_thickness` with a centered `cylinder` peg of height `stick_length`. Composite blocks (two-block, three-block, corner-block, four-block) are assembled by translating and unioning multiple instances of this single block. The baseplate and baseplate holes are generated using a `difference` operation between a solid thin `cube` and a nested grid loop of `CreateBasePlateHole` modules, which subtract square socket shapes using `cube` primitives.
